The main takeaway from our work is that
SEDEX sequential extraction is a viable instrument to study the nutrient supply in fossil carbonate systems.

the SEDEX sequential extraction can be applied to fossil carbonates, allowing to reconstruct the nutrient influence on carbonate factories and to better interpret the palaeoecological patterns of ancient oceans.

the SEDEX sequential extraction can be a useful tool to study the palaeo-nitrogen and phosphorus levels in the geological record, providing a powerful instrument to investigate the role of nutrients on carbonate-factories in the past.
